messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@telemed.com>, Sally Huang <sally.huang@telemed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: TeleMed network & compliance interlock — technical recap and asks

Thanks again for carving out time earlier today. Short recap of what we heard and the concrete asks so everyone is aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you emphasized:
- Data must remain within TeleMed-controlled VPCs in us-west-2; no model weights or raw PHI may persist in any third-party storage.
- Regulatory driver: California state telehealth rules + upcoming payer audit — they require strict audit trails and customer-managed KMS.
- Network: TeleMed will only allow egress to fixed IPs; they plan to restrict outbound via NAT gateway + strict firewall rules.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Proof-of-concept: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC peering) serving non-identifiable clinical summaries by end of Q3.
2) An operator-run plan for auditability: KMS/HSM integration, retention policy, and detailed access logs.
3) Clear acceptance criteria for connectivity and security so the procurement team can sign the SOW.

Technical constraints and notes from the call:
- No internet egress from the model runtime aside from a small set of CIDR/IP ranges (we documented the requirement to whitelist).
- TeleMed will not permit external object storage for model caches; Redwood's runtime will need to use ephemeral local NVMe and customer-provided KV-store within the VPC.
- Access controls: all service-to-service auth will be via mTLS + client certificate, and TeleMed requires CA-based certs.

Asks / next steps (owner / ETA):
- TeleMed: confirm final egress IPs and preferred CA for client certs (Rajesh / by Tue 5/18).
- Redwood: share private deployment checklist + proposed network diagram (Jordan / today 5/14) — attached.
- Redwood: produce a short note on KMS integration options (Vivek / by Fri 5/21).
- Both: schedule a narrow technical interlock with TeleMed networking & security (30–45m) to agree on firewall rules and peering specifics (Laura to coordinate / by 5/19).

Attachments: telemed_network_requirements_v1.pdf (requirements I sketched during the call), redwood_private_architecture_sketch.png (high-level private deployment flow).

Best,
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: TeleMed network & compliance interlock — technical recap and asks

Thanks Jordan — helpful summary. Couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) Egress: we will provide an allowlist of /32 IPs for the first phase (expected by 5/18). Can you confirm Redwood needs explicit CIDR or can accept a CIDR list?
2) Storage: we cannot accept any persistent cache outside our VPC. Ephemeral NVMe for model KV is acceptable, but does Redwood require any stateful object store for checkpoints or retraining artifacts? We will not approve such storage.
3) KMS: TeleMed uses an internal AWS KMS key tied to our account; we can provide either an external KMS proxy or grant Redwood a role to call Encrypt/Decrypt — we need a short options note to route to security.

Procurement is looped for SOW questions. Also looping in our networking lead if needed for the interlock.

-Rajesh
Dr. Rajesh Patel
CTO, TeleMed Health
rajesh.patel@telemed.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@telemed.com>, Sally Huang <sally.huang@telemed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@telemed.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TeleMed network & compliance interlock — technical recap and asks

Rajesh — thanks, and good questions. Answers inline below and a very small request set so your networking/security can review quickly.

1) Egress allowlist: Redwood is flexible — we can accept either explicit /32s or a CIDR set. For our runtime we prefer stable IPs; providing /32s is ideal.

2) Storage/checkpoints: Redwood's private runtime does not require external persistent object storage for production inference. The only optional artifacts are non-sensitive model checkpoint exports for offline retraining (we will not pull any PHI). For the POC we will disable checkpoint exports entirely. Confirmed: no third-party storage will be used.

3) KMS integration options (high level):
   - Option A: Role-based access to TeleMed's AWS KMS (recommended) — Redwood assumes an IAM role scoped to encrypt/decrypt operations; logs remain in your account.
   - Option B: Customer-provided KMS proxy (we call a local endpoint in your VPC).
   - Option C: HSM integration (longer lead, for HIPAA-level requirements).

We captured the minimal technical whitelist we need for the runtime control plane and for package/image pulls during initial bootstrap (we can avoid runtime outbound after bootstrap if you prefer). Summary attached and pasted below for quick review.

Minimal firewall items (suggested):
- Outbound 1: TCP 443 to 3 IPs for initial bootstrap (image registry) — we can replace with offline images if blocked.
- Outbound 2: TCP 443 to control-plane endpoints (optionally via Transit Gateway) — configurable.
- mTLS: client CA certs validated on connection.

Next steps:
- Rajesh: deliver the /32 list + preferred CA by EOD 5/18.
- Laura: can you propose three windows for a 45m interlock next week (include networking/security)?
- Vivek: I asked product to prepare a short KMS memo — please have that ready by Fri 5/21.

If helpful I can prepare a short diagram that shows where keys live and where logs are written (no PHI flows outside your VPC).

Best,
Jordan
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Internal: TeleMed interlock prep (notes for security interlock)

Quick internal note after Rajesh's reply — preparing the deck and checklist for the interlock. TL;DR:
- Confirm we will proceed with Option A (role-based KMS) as our default ask; Option B as fall-back. Vivek: draft the 1‑page KMS choices doc.
- Prepare an image-bootstrap offline workflow in case TeleMed blocks initial registry egress — Laura, can you add an ops play for offline image install to the checklist?
- Inventory of logs we will provide to TeleMed for audit (access logs, request IDs, token-level latency) — I'll pull last-quarter samples to show what we surface.

I'll attach the two files I sent externally to the interlock invite. Planning to propose Tue/Wed next week windows.

-Jordan
